::: {#exm-hers-nested-models}
#### Nested models for fasting glucose in HERS

In the HERS data, take the linear regression of `glucose` on `BMI` as the smaller model.
The [larger model](#def-nested-regression-models) adds `age` and `exercise`, so $q = 2$:

$$
\begin{aligned}
  \text{smaller:}\quad \mean(\text{glucose})
    &= \intcoef + \coef{\text{BMI}} \cdot \text{BMI}, \\
  \text{larger:}\quad \mean(\text{glucose})
    &= \intcoef + \coef{\text{BMI}} \cdot \text{BMI}
      + \coef{\text{age}} \cdot \text{age}
      + \coef{\text{exercise}} \cdot \text{exercise}.
\end{aligned}
$$

Both models must be fitted to the same HERS participants,
so keep the participants with all four variables measured:

```{r}
#| label: hers-nested-fits
#| code-fold: false
hers_nested <- hers |>
  tidyr::drop_na(glucose, BMI, age, exercise)
fit_smaller <- lm(glucose ~ BMI, data = hers_nested)
fit_larger <- lm(glucose ~ BMI + age + exercise, data = hers_nested)
nrow(hers_nested)
```

The smaller model sets $\coef{\text{age}} = \coef{\text{exercise}} = 0$ in the larger one.
:::
